Hi sir, first of all, I genuinely appreciate your content and the effort you put into your videos. I enjoy watching your perspectives, and that’s why I wanted to ask something with complete respect and just for clarity.

You often introduce yourself as the “CEO of secularism,” and I wanted to understand how you differentiate your approach from creators like Dhruv Rathee. The reason I ask is because, from an audience perspective, many of your videos seem heavily critical of parties like Congress and AAP, while sounding comparatively supportive of BJP.

So my question is: what makes your position different from someone you criticize for being politically inclined? From the outside, it can sometimes feel less like a neutral secular stance and more like a pro-BJP narrative.

For example, when topics like Hindutva come up repeatedly, it feels slightly disconnected from the secular positioning mentioned in your introduction. I’m not saying you shouldn’t criticize Congress or praise BJP where deserved — every party has strengths and weaknesses — but I rarely see balanced appreciation or criticism across the spectrum, and that creates confusion for viewers like me.

I also wanted your perspective on India’s economic direction. A lot has been said about India becoming the fourth-largest economy, but there are also concerns regarding currency value, economic pressure, unemployment, and comparisons with previous finance ministers during difficult economic periods. It would genuinely be interesting to hear a detailed, fact-based analysis from you on these topics as well.

Another thing I struggle to understand is this: BJP itself has had multiple leaders and ministers over the years who have faced serious allegations of corruption, criminal activity, hate speech, or misconduct. There are also many instances where candidates are criticised for lacking qualifications, education, or basic professionalism in public office. So when you strongly defend the party while positioning yourself as a secular and highly informed commentator, it becomes difficult for viewers like me to fully understand that balance.

And honestly, that’s where my confusion comes from. You come across as a well-read, educated, and informed person, which is exactly why I’m curious about how you reconcile these contradictions in your own narrative.
